eed39640-21ea-46ab-ac54-c61e40eae1e0.hook_pattern: Simple human truth demolishes tech hubris — plain-language counter-reply outperforms the original post
eed39640-21ea-46ab-ac54-c61e40eae1e0.hook_template: What if you just [obvious human thing]?
eed39640-21ea-46ab-ac54-c61e40eae1e0.psychological_trigger: Moral indignation + humor + identity threat (anti-AI-replacement sentiment triggered by CEO overreach)
eed39640-21ea-46ab-ac54-c61e40eae1e0.structural_lesson: A CEO made a grand AI product pitch. A creator with cultural credibility replied with a single rhetorical question in plain language. The reply generated 13x more likes than the original. The simpler, more human the counter-statement, the harder it lands on an audience primed for tech skepticism.

7be960fd-25de-440a-8959-a54c9fc9cd69.hook_pattern: PSA escalation with expanding scope — 'call your friends' urgency that grows across multiple updates
7be960fd-25de-440a-8959-a54c9fc9cd69.hook_template: ⚠️ PSA: If you used [product/tool] before [date], your [asset] may be at risk. Check now.
7be960fd-25de-440a-8959-a54c9fc9cd69.psychological_trigger: Fear + social responsibility (protecting others) + FOMO (am I affected?) + serial anxiety (each update reveals more damage)
7be960fd-25de-440a-8959-a54c9fc9cd69.structural_lesson: What started as a 594 BTC theft became $89M across 4,585 addresses in three escalating waves. Each wave spawned a new viral update thread. The 'call your friends' framing transformed personal financial fear into communal protection behavior, triggering sharing from people who didn't even own Coldcards. Ongoing crises that escalate in scope generate compounding engagement across multiple news cycles.

6fbffe92-de9a-48af-9100-cfc836c25470.hook_pattern: Reframe of a familiar action as a hidden tax — reveals that something the audience does innocently is actually exploiting them
6fbffe92-de9a-48af-9100-cfc836c25470.hook_template: You pay for [X] twice. Once with [obvious cost]. And again with [hidden cost] most people never realize.
6fbffe92-de9a-48af-9100-cfc836c25470.psychological_trigger: Betrayal + loss aversion + identity threat to decision-makers (am I being played?)
6fbffe92-de9a-48af-9100-cfc836c25470.structural_lesson: Satya Nadella's 'you pay for AI twice' framing — money and proprietary knowledge — spread widely because it reframed a normal business decision (using AI) as an unnoticed exploitation. The hook works because it implies the audience is already a victim, which triggers both urgency and sharing (warning others). Authority figure (CEO of Microsoft) giving the warning adds legitimacy that makes it impossible to dismiss.

bfdff026-c27a-485d-b406-99925268344e.hook_pattern: Authority self-contradiction — when the person who sold you the hype admits it isn't working
bfdff026-c27a-485d-b406-99925268344e.hook_template: The CEO who spent $[amount] on [thing] just admitted [thing] is not working as expected.
bfdff026-c27a-485d-b406-99925268344e.psychological_trigger: Schadenfreude + validation of skepticism + I-told-you-so (reward for those who doubted the hype)
bfdff026-c27a-485d-b406-99925268344e.structural_lesson: Zuckerberg telling staff AI agent development is slower than expected — despite laying off 10% of staff and spending $145B on AI infrastructure — became massively shareable because it validated the private doubts of a huge audience. Posts where the highest-profile believers admit shortfall give permission to every skeptic to say 'I knew it.' The contrast between capital deployed and results admitted is the structural engine.

949d4115-d4dc-4a01-a3ff-27412660d652.hook_pattern: Dueling definitions that make both sides right — viral debate where neither party can definitively win because they're arguing about different things
949d4115-d4dc-4a01-a3ff-27412660d652.hook_template: Expert A says [bold claim]. Expert B says [direct contradiction]. They're both right — and that's the problem.
949d4115-d4dc-4a01-a3ff-27412660d652.psychological_trigger: Intellectual tribalism + identity investment in the outcome + curiosity gap (who's actually right?)
949d4115-d4dc-4a01-a3ff-27412660d652.structural_lesson: The Brockman '70% to AGI' vs. Gary Marcus 'trillion-dollar delusion' debate spread because both are arguing from different definitions of AGI. Posts that frame irreconcilable expert disagreements as stemming from definitional differences generate threads because people feel compelled to pick a side. The debate format invites participation in a way that a single opinion never does. Leave the resolution ambiguous — conclusion-free debates outperform ones with a clear winner.

7fe64698-0192-40c1-ae93-c6dc44d1e7fb.hook_pattern: Specific metric + compressed timeframe + single tool — the credibility triple that makes 'I built this' posts viral
7fe64698-0192-40c1-ae93-c6dc44d1e7fb.hook_template: [$X ARR] in [N days/weeks]. No engineers. Just [tool]. Here's exactly how I did it.
7fe64698-0192-40c1-ae93-c6dc44d1e7fb.psychological_trigger: Inspiration + FOMO + proof of concept (if they can do it, so can I) + concrete specificity (not vague, not aspirational — numbers)
7fe64698-0192-40c1-ae93-c6dc44d1e7fb.structural_lesson: Vibe coding founder posts went viral in this cycle because they combined three credibility signals: a real revenue number, a shockingly compressed timeframe, and attribution to a single specific tool. Vague 'I built a business with AI' posts perform poorly. '456K ARR in 45 days using Lovable' performs well. The tool name does double work — it provides specificity AND free promotion from the tool's community. End with a thread breakdown to capture follow engagement.

0044452a-3f7f-4101-8431-6048aa5d6f01.hook_pattern: Data-point flippening as tribal provocation — a single stat that forces two communities into conflict
0044452a-3f7f-4101-8431-6048aa5d6f01.hook_template: [Token A] just overtook [Token B] in [metric]. The [Metric] flippening is already here.
0044452a-3f7f-4101-8431-6048aa5d6f01.psychological_trigger: Tribalism + identity threat (for the losing side) + social proof (for the winning side) + confirmation bias
0044452a-3f7f-4101-8431-6048aa5d6f01.structural_lesson: XRP overtaking Ethereum in X mentions generated engagement from both XRP and ETH holders simultaneously — one tribe celebrating, one defending. Data-point posts that trigger opposing communities are structurally superior to posts that only appeal to one. The 'flippening' framing has tribal mythology built in and requires no context — it lands instantly with crypto-native audiences. Use recognized tribal language that already carries emotional charge.

b8af560e-5c88-4b8f-b5c0-a6bed06d503d.hook_pattern: Ongoing crisis with a new chapter — the 'goodwill plan reveal' update that reactivates a dormant news cycle
b8af560e-5c88-4b8f-b5c0-a6bed06d503d.hook_template: UPDATE: [Protocol] just revealed its plan for the [N] affected users. Here's what happens next.
b8af560e-5c88-4b8f-b5c0-a6bed06d503d.psychological_trigger: Stakes + ongoing drama + resolution curiosity (will they be made whole?) + moral judgment (is 30% bounty fair?)
b8af560e-5c88-4b8f-b5c0-a6bed06d503d.structural_lesson: AFX Trade's $24M hack generated three viral moments: (1) the initial hack, (2) the 30% bounty offer to the hacker, and (3) the goodwill plan reveal for affected users on August 3. Each chapter reactivated the audience. The structural lesson: protocols that handle crises publicly and show their next steps get more engagement than those that go dark. The 'bounty offer to hacker' framing is uniquely crypto-native and triggers moral outrage + curiosity simultaneously.
